"Unstable Equilibrium" posits that small changes in neural excitation can cause complete behavioral derailment, akin to a ball balanced on a hilltop. "Pathological Unlocking" introduces a permanent architectural defect that removes safety constraints, allowing any stimulus to trigger an inappropriate response. Finally, "Capricious Will" captures the resulting erratic preference reversal, where stable aversions evaporate instantly upon exposure to temptation. Together, they form a predictive triad: a susceptible system (UE), a broken brake (PU), and unpredictable outcomes (CW). In GSI, this maps to markets that are primed for flash crashes or irrational bubbles. In GSE, it models agents trapped in non-stationary environments where Q-learning fails to converge.
